subject: Shiv Sena’s protest, and the growing demand for ‘Belonging’
alt: Hemant Bagoriya’s cartoon: two panels, with the title ‘Reaction of Shivsena’ written by hand at the top. At the left a large tiger leans forward, eyes narrowed in anger, fangs bared, both paws pressed on a square book or tablet marked ‘BELONGINGS’ in thick letters, with claw marks across it. At the right stands a penguin with a large eye and beak, a black body and a white belly; it holds up a large book whose cover reads ‘BELONGINGS’ and, below, ‘Sona Gandhi’. Human hands grip the book from above and below. The background is plain white, with grey shadows at the bottom.
chutki: On the left, Shiv Sena’s tiger presses down on the book and tears it with its paws; on the right, a penguin holds the same book up with a smile while hands reach in from all sides to grab it.

The needle is that the party’s protest turned into publicity for the book. The harder it was torn, the more it was talked about; the noise of the protest sent people towards the book, and the penguin’s smile only grew. Shiv Sena’s ‘reaction’ to Sonia Gandhi’s book became an advertisement for the book itself.
